facts.label: Application
facts.text: 15 October, 09:00 – 5 November 2026, 17:00 JST, online. Application fee ¥17,000.

facts.label: What is assessed
facts.text: Two essays, a video assignment, school transcripts, one standardized test or qualification, an English test and an online interview for those who pass the first screening.

facts.label: Tests
facts.text: Expected, not cut-off: SAT 1480 or above, or ACT 33 or above, without superscoring; IB, A-levels and other designated qualifications are alternatives.

facts.label: English
facts.text: Expectations: IELTS Academic greater than 6.0, TOEFL iBT greater than 80 (or greater than 4 on the scale used from 21 January 2026), Duolingo greater than 110, Cambridge greater than 169.

funding.text: UTokyo Design Needs-Based Scholarship (¥2,400,000 a year plus the admission fee equivalent, up to five years) and Merit-Based Scholarship (¥600,000 a year), both open regardless of nationality.

routes.name: PEAK (Programs in English at Komaba)
routes.forWhom: No longer open to new applicants.
routes.summary: Historical information. The University of Tokyo stated that the September 2026 enrolment was the last recruitment for PEAK and that applications are closed; no PEAK intake is offered for 2027.

facts.label: Selection, when it ran
facts.text: Documentary and interview-based screening through the Admissions Office entrance examination.

facts.label: Scholarships published for PEAK
facts.text: The MEXT scholarship could be offered to up to five successful international applicants (admission fee, tuition, ¥120,000 a month and round-trip airfare), and country-specific scholarships existed for students from Vietnam and Indonesia. These were for PEAK applicants and are not offered to College of Design applicants on the pages read.

funding.text: The route is closed, so its scholarships cannot be applied for.

routes.note: The PEAK site did not answer on 11 October 2026; the university's page on English-taught undergraduate programmes read that day lists only the Global Science Course.

routes.name: Global Science Course (GSC)
routes.forWhom: Transfer students who have already completed at least two years of undergraduate study at a university outside Japan. It is not a route straight from school.
routes.summary: An all-English transfer programme: students enter the third year of the Faculty of Science and graduate with a Bachelor of Science.

facts.label: Schedule
facts.text: Guidelines by late December; applications from late January to late March; document screening and an online interview in April–May; decisions by early June; enrolment in October. No dated schedule for the next period was published on the page read.

funding.text: The university states that all GSC transfer students receive a monthly scholarship of ¥150,000 and accommodation with the monthly rent fully supported.
